symptomShortText: Coating peel found at customer incoming inspection

causesIshikawa.description: EMP-3402, Shift A - line settings matched the released recipe
EQ-COAT05-003, gun voltage and powder flow logged within band
DOC-6044 Rev C - powder coating recipe, unchanged since 2025-11
Powder lot PWD-2231 within shelf life, cert PASS
Thickness gauge GA-0117 calibration expired 2026-05-30; re-calibration on 2026-08-04 confirmed a -22um reading drift, so under-coated parts were passing as in-spec

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did the coating peel at the customer?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Coating thickness measured 38um against a 60-90um spec, giving cross-cut adhesion Class 3 instead of Class 0-1

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did under-coated parts pass in-house inspection?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Thickness gauge GA-0117 read 22um high, so a 38um coat was recorded as 60um and accepted

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was a drifting gauge still in service? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: GA-0117 calibration expired on 2026-05-30 and no interlock stops an expired gauge from being used for release decisions

actions.actionText: Remove GA-0117 from service and re-measure all C80 stock with calibrated gauge GA-0103
Contain 74 units at the customer plant and arrange sorting on site
Re-calibrate GA-0117 and re-inspect every C80 lot released since 2026-05-30

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Comparing the two coating lines isolated the gauge as the only difference within one shift
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Nothing prevented an expired gauge from being used for release - the calibration due date was advisory only

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: C80 covers - WC-COAT-05 - parts released against gauge GA-0117 after 2026-05-30
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: C60 covers - WC-COAT-02 - released against gauge GA-0103, calibration current
isIsNot.notes: Defect follows the gauge, not the powder lot or the line settings
